memory_candidates.content: A fixture-building test suite that seals a synthetic .claude/scripts/lib/ tree via a hardcoded file-copy allowlist (e.g. REQUIRED_LIB_SCRIPTS=(...)) will silently go stale whenever a new shared library is added to the real lib/ directory -- nothing mechanically keeps the allowlist in sync. Symptom: 'state-write.sh: line N: .../lib/<new-lib>.sh: No such file or directory' inside the fixture, reproducing identically in total isolation. Before attributing such a failure to in-flight changes, grep the failing suite for its own hardcoded lib-copy array and check whether the missing library predates the current dispatch (git log --format=%ct on the library file vs. dispatch_start_ts).

For a lint that bidirectionally diffs a markdown table's first column against a real directory set, give it a single optional positional ROOT argument (reading <root>/README.md and enumerating <root>/*/ from that same root) rather than two independent path flags. This single-root input contract makes a regression suite trivial: one mktemp scratch directory, varying only its README table rows and subdirectory set, covers every case (clean, missing row, extra row, an exemption case) with one fixture helper.

Adding a new gate to a dynamically-dispatched gate registry (gate_registry_ids + "gate${id}_run" lookup) requires only a gate-registry.data row plus the new gate<N>_run function -- no call-site list to edit. But it DOES require bumping hardcoded gate-count/max-id assertions in sibling regression suites that pin the registry's exact shape (e.g. test-gate-registry-resolution.sh's expected-id-count and live-max/one-past-max probes, test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh's out-of-range probe and `seq 1 N` loop). This is expected, recurring maintenance on every gate addition, not scope creep, and should be anticipated rather than discovered as a surprise test failure.
